title: Time
about: Collocations with the word time (spend, waste, save and kill time, take your time, bang on time, run out of time) and phrases for talking about the past and the future, such as the small hours, from dawn till dusk and in the not too distant future.

parts.title: More with day, hour, clock and minute
parts.note: Завдання з книжки: знайти у словнику по два сполучення до day, hour, clock і minute. Ось ті, що трапляються найчастіше. Зверни увагу: «переводити годинник» — put the clocks back / forward, «Маєш хвилинку?» — Have you got a minute? або Can you spare a minute?, а «зрештою» в розмові часто звучить як at the end of the day.

rows: We set off just as day was breaking, and the roads were still empty.
at the end of the day
At the end of the day, it's your money, so you decide.
Grandad loves talking about the good old days, when a bus ticket cost ten pence.
In this day and age, it's strange that the village still has no bus service.
The boat trip lasts an hour and leaves from the pier every afternoon.
With every passing hour, the queue outside the new bakery got longer.
працювати в незручний час (ночами, у вихідні) / за звичайним графіком
Nurses often work anti-social hours, but my sister prefers to work regular hours in an office.
After the night flight I slept for ten solid hours.
The church clock struck twelve just as we got home.
раз у раз дивитися на годинник (чекати кінця роботи)
On Friday afternoons everyone in the office starts to watch the clock.
Don't forget we put the clocks back this weekend, so you can sleep an hour longer.
The quiz host stopped the clock while the contestant had a drink of water.
The minutes ticked by as we waited outside the operating theatre.
Have you got a minute? / Can you spare a minute?
Have you got a minute? I need some advice about my car.
Hold on a minute, I'll just get my coat.
Ring me the minute you get home.

items.pattern: spend time (with sb / doing sth / in a place) · spend a week / an evening somewhere · spend – spent – spent
items.meaning: use a period of time in a particular place, with someone or doing something
items.example: My grandparents **spend a lot of time** in their garden in summer.
more: I'd love to **spend more time** with my kids, but I work late most days.
She **spent** most of her **time** at the seaside reading and swimming.
items.watchOut: «Проводити час» — spend time. Не hold і не conduct: так «проводять» збори чи дослідження (hold a meeting). Pass the time кажуть, коли треба чимось заповнити нудне очікування: We played cards to pass the time. А «гарно провести час» — have a good time, не spend a good time.

items.pattern: waste time (on sth / doing sth) · a waste of time · waste money / energy
items.meaning: use time badly, on something that is not useful or doesn't bring results
items.example: Don't **waste time** ironing towels: nobody will notice.
more: I **wasted** the whole evening watching rubbish on TV.
That meeting was a complete **waste of time**: nothing was decided.
items.watchOut: «Марнувати час» — waste time. Lose time зазвичай кажуть, коли час забрали обставини: We lost an hour in a traffic jam. «Марна трата часу» — a waste of time, з of.

items.pattern: save time (by doing sth) · save sb time · save an hour · save money · time-saving
items.meaning: do something in a quicker way so that you need less time
items.example: You'll **save time** if you chop all the vegetables before you start cooking.
more: A monthly bus pass **saves** me **time**: I don't have to queue for a ticket every morning.
We **saved** a lot of **time** by taking a taxi instead of waiting for the bus.
items.watchOut: «Економити час» — save time, не economise time: economise кажуть про гроші чи ресурси (economise on heating). Save тут означає «заощаджувати», а не «рятувати».

items.pattern: tell sb the time · (can) tell the time = read a clock · Have you got the time?
items.meaning: say what time it is now; (can) tell the time = be able to read a clock
items.uk: сказати, котра година; (вміти) визначати час за годинником
items.example: Excuse me, could you **tell me the time**? My phone's dead.
more: I don't need a fancy watch: one that **tells the time** is enough.
The kitchen clock has no numbers, so it's quite hard to **tell the time** at a glance.
items.watchOut: «Котра година?» — Could you tell me the time?, не tell me the hour. Have you got the time? (з the) — «Котра година?», а Have you got time? (без the) — «У тебе є час?»

items.pattern: (in) your free / spare time · leisure time (more formal) · have little free time
items.meaning: time when you are not working or studying and can do what you like
items.example: In her **spare time** Oksana makes jewellery and sells it at the market.
more: I don't have much **free time** during the week, so I do the shopping on Saturdays.
My dad spends most of his **spare time** fishing at the lake.
items.watchOut: «У вільний час» — in my / your free time, з in і зазвичай із присвійним займенником. Spare — «запасний, зайвий» (a spare key), тож spare time — час, що лишається після роботи. Leisure time звучить книжніше.

items.pattern: have (no) time to do sth · have time for sth · have no time for sb (= no patience with sb)
items.meaning: have enough time to do something; have no time for sb = not like someone or have no patience with them
items.example: I didn't **have time to** wash my hair this morning, so I put it in a ponytail.
more: We won't **have time for** lunch if the meeting runs late.
My grandmother **has no time for** people who are rude to waiters.
items.watchOut: «Я не встиг це зробити» часто звучить як I didn't have time to do it, з інфінітивом (have time for doing звучить неприродно). А have no time for sb — не про розклад, а «не терпіти когось, не мати до когось терпіння».

items.pattern: make time for sb / sth · make time to do sth · also find time
items.meaning: find time for someone or something even though you are busy
items.example: However busy she is, Mum always **makes time for** a walk in the evening.
more: You should **make time for** your friends, not just for your job.
The head teacher promised to **make time to** see us on Friday.
items.watchOut: «Знайти час для когось» — make time for sb (можна й find time). Make тут означає «створити». Не do time: do time — «відбувати строк у в'язниці».

items.pattern: kill time (doing sth) · kill an hour / half an hour · also pass the time
items.meaning: do something to fill the time while you are waiting for something you have planned
items.example: Our flight was delayed, so we **killed time** looking round the duty-free shops.
more: I got to the cinema early and **killed** half an hour in a café across the road.
We played word games to **pass the time** on the long car journey.
items.watchOut: Kill time — заповнити час, поки чекаєш на щось заплановане. Якщо ж час іде даремно, коли є справи, — waste time. «Скоротати час» — ще й pass the time, зазвичай з the.

items.pattern: take your / his / our time (over sth / doing sth) · Take your time! · take time (= need a long time)
items.meaning: do something slowly and carefully, without hurrying
items.uk: не поспішати, робити щось без поспіху
items.example: There's no rush: **take your time** and choose the dress you really like.
more: The waiter told us to **take our time** over the menu.
He **took his time** replying: the letter came three months later.
items.watchOut: «Не поспішай!» — Take your time!, з your (my, his…). Без присвійного take time означає «потребувати часу»: Getting used to a new school takes time.

items.pattern: bang / dead / right on time · (just) on time · in time (= early enough)
items.meaning: exactly at the planned time; bang and dead are very informal
items.example: The taxi came **bang on time**, so we didn't have to wait in the rain.
more: Our bus is usually late, but this morning it came **right on time**.
The guests turned up **dead on time**, just as the roast came out of the oven.
items.watchOut: On time — за розкладом, не пізніше; in time — завчасно, щоб устигнути: We got there in time to buy popcorn. «Точно вчасно» — bang / dead / right on time; bang і dead — дуже розмовні.

items.pattern: have a good / great / lovely / terrible time (doing sth) · Have a good time!
items.meaning: enjoy yourself (or not) on an occasion
items.example: We **had a great time** at my cousin's wedding: we danced until midnight.
more: **Have a good time** in Lviv, and send us some photos!
Did the kids **have a good time** at the zoo?
items.watchOut: «Гарно провести час» — have a good time, не spend a good time. Spend time — просто проводити час десь, без оцінки: We spent a week in Spain.

items.phrase: have the time of your life
items.pattern: have the time of your / his / her / their life (lives)
items.meaning: enjoy yourself more than ever before
items.uk: чудово провести час, як ніколи в житті
items.example: The children **had the time of their lives** at the water park.
more: My grandmother **had the time of her life** on her first cruise at the age of eighty.
If you go to the festival, you'll **have the time of your life**.
items.watchOut: Займенник змінюється: I had the time of my life, they had the time of their lives. The best time of my life — інше: «найкращий період життя» (University was the best time of my life).

items.phrase: as time goes by / as time passes
items.pattern: as time goes by / goes on / passes · as time went by (in stories about the past)
items.meaning: gradually, as days, months and years pass
items.example: The old house felt cold and strange, but **as time went by** it began to feel like home.
more: **As time passes**, you'll forget all about this silly argument.
The pain in my knee got better **as time went by**.
items.watchOut: «З часом» — as time goes by (passes), over time або in time. У розповіді про минуле дієслово теж у минулому: as time went by. А «час летить» — time flies.

items.pattern: run out of time (money, milk, petrol) · time is running out · run – ran – run
items.meaning: have no time left to finish something
items.example: We **ran out of time** before we could see the castle, so we'll go back next year.
more: Hurry up, we're **running out of time**: the shop closes at six.
The builders **ran out of time**, and the kitchen wasn't ready for Christmas.
items.watchOut: «Мені не вистачило часу» — I ran out of time, з of. Не ran off time: run off — «утекти». Так само run out of milk, money, petrol.

items.pattern: verb + big time (informal, at the end) · owe sb big time · mess up big time
items.meaning: very much; extremely (informal)
items.example: I messed up **big time**: I forgot my sister's birthday.
more: After the argument, Tom apologised **big time**, with flowers and chocolates.
If Dad finds out you scratched his car, you'll be in trouble **big time**.
items.watchOut: Big time — розмовне, стоїть у кінці речення: You owe me big time. Це не «великий час». У листі чи офіційній розмові краще very much або a great deal.

items.pattern: the past / last few weeks (days, months, years) · for / over the past few weeks · often with the present perfect
items.meaning: the period of a few weeks up to now
items.example: It has rained almost every day for **the past few weeks**.
more: **The past few days** have been really busy at work.
Food prices have gone up a lot over **the last few months**.
items.watchOut: «Останні тижні» — the past / last few weeks, зазвичай із present perfect: I've felt tired for the past few weeks. Не the latest weeks: latest — «найновіший» (the latest news).

items.pattern: the early / mid / late 21st (19th, 20th…) century · in the early / late 1990s · early 21st-century fiction (before a noun)
items.meaning: the first years of the 21st century
items.example: Our block of flats was built in **the early 21st century**, so it's still quite modern.
more: My great-grandparents' farmhouse dates from **the late 19th century**.
She's writing a book about **early 20th-century** fashion.
items.watchOut: «На початку XXI століття» — in the early 21st (twenty-first) century, з the. At the beginning of the 21st century теж правильно, але довше. Так само in the late 1990s — «наприкінці 90-х».

items.pattern: in / since prehistoric times · in ancient / medieval / Roman times
items.meaning: the very distant past, before people wrote down history
items.example: People were already living in these caves in **prehistoric times**.
more: The museum has stone tools from **prehistoric times**.
In **medieval times**, this little street was the town's main market.
items.watchOut: «У доісторичні часи» — in prehistoric times: з in і times у множині. Так само in ancient / medieval / Roman times.

items.pattern: in the recent past · the distant past · in the past
items.meaning: a time not long ago
items.example: Our neighbourhood has changed a lot in **the recent past**: there are three new cafés.
more: Several shops in our street have closed in **the recent past**.
Grandad prefers stories from **the distant past** to anything that happened last week.
items.watchOut: «Недавнє (недалеке) минуле» — the recent past, з the; the near past так зазвичай не кажуть. «Далеке минуле» — the distant past.

items.pattern: set your / the alarm (for six o'clock) · set an alarm on your phone · set – set – set
items.meaning: make an alarm clock ready to ring at a certain time
items.example: I **set my alarm** for half past five so I wouldn't miss the early train.
more: Don't forget to **set the alarm** before you go to sleep.
She **sets an alarm** on her phone to remind her to take her tablets.
items.watchOut: «Поставити будильник» — set the alarm, не put the alarm. Put — просто поставити річ кудись: Put the alarm clock on the shelf.

items.pattern: an alarm goes off (rings) · a car / fire / burglar alarm goes off · a timer goes off · go – went – gone
items.meaning: an alarm starts ringing or making a loud noise
items.example: When **the alarm went off** at six, I pressed snooze and went back to sleep.
more: Our neighbours' burglar **alarm went off** while they were on holiday, and nobody could turn it off.
A car **alarm went off** in the car park and wouldn't stop.
items.watchOut: «Задзвонив будильник» — the alarm went off (або rang), не called. Ring off — «покласти слухавку». Go off — ще й «вибухнути» (бомба) та «зіпсуватися» (молоко).

items.pattern: from dawn till / until / to dusk
items.meaning: all day, from early morning until it gets dark
items.uk: від світанку до смеркання, з ранку до вечора
items.example: During the harvest, my uncle works in the fields **from dawn till dusk**.
more: In summer the kids played outside **from dawn till dusk**.
We walked **from dawn to dusk** and covered thirty kilometres.
items.watchOut: Порядок саме такий: from dawn till dusk (світанок → сутінки). From dusk till dawn — навпаки, «всю ніч». Dawn /dɔːn/ — не /daʊn/, як down.

items.pattern: in / until / into the small hours (of the morning) · also the early hours
items.meaning: the hours just after midnight, around 1, 2 or 3 a.m.
items.uk: глибока ніч, перші години після опівночі
items.example: Our neighbours' party went on into **the small hours**.
more: The baby woke up in **the small hours** and wouldn't go back to sleep.
We sat in the kitchen talking until **the small hours**.
items.watchOut: The small hours — не «малі години», а глибока ніч, десь з першої до четвертої. Те саме — the early hours (of the morning). «До глибокої ночі» — until the small hours або late into the night, а не until deep night.

items.pattern: at an / this ungodly hour · work / keep ungodly hours · also an unearthly hour
items.meaning: an unreasonably early or late time of day (informal, used when complaining)
items.example: Cheap flights often leave at **ungodly hours**, like five in the morning.
more: My brother phoned at some **ungodly hour** to tell us his wife had had the baby.
Our neighbour starts mowing his lawn at an **ungodly hour** every Saturday.
items.watchOut: Ungodly hour — розмовне, коли скаржаться, що надто рано чи надто пізно; до релігії тут стосунку немає. Синонім — unearthly hour. Про роботу ночами й у вихідні офіційніше кажуть unsociable hours.

items.pattern: it takes (sb) ages to do sth · sth takes ages · for ages (= for a long time)
items.meaning: need a very long time (informal)
items.example: It **took me ages** to find a parking space near the hospital.
more: The kettle **takes ages** to boil in this old flat.
It **takes ages** to get through security at this airport.
items.watchOut: «Цілу вічність» у розмові — ages, у множині й зазвичай без артикля: It took ages (британці іноді кажуть an age). I haven't seen you for ages — «Сто років тебе не бачив».

items.pattern: be worth sb's while (to do sth / doing sth) · make it worth sb's while · worthwhile (adjective)
items.meaning: worth the time and effort you spend on it
items.example: The museum is a bit far from the centre, but it's well **worth your while** to go.
more: If you help me move the piano, I'll **make it worth your while**.
It isn't **worth my while** driving into town just for a loaf of bread.
items.watchOut: Worth your / my / their while — з присвійним займенником, не worth the while. Простіше — it's worth it. Worthwhile — одним словом, прикметник: a worthwhile trip.

items.phrase: have a great future ahead of you
items.pattern: have a great / bright future ahead of you (him, her) · have your whole life ahead of you
items.meaning: be likely to be very successful in the future
items.example: Your daughter sings beautifully: she **has a great future ahead of her**.
more: The coach thinks the young goalkeeper **has a bright future ahead of him**.
You're only nineteen and you **have your whole life ahead of you**, so don't worry about one bad exam.
items.watchOut: «Світле майбутнє» — a bright future, не a light future. «Попереду» — ahead of you; кажуть і in front of you, а before you звучить книжно.

items.phrase: in the not too distant future
items.pattern: in the not too distant future · in the near future · in the distant future
items.meaning: quite soon, but not immediately
items.uk: у не надто далекому майбутньому, незабаром
items.example: We hope to buy a house of our own **in the not too distant future**.
more: I'd love to visit Japan **in the not too distant future**.
The bridge will be closed for repairs **in the near future**.
items.watchOut: Порядок слів: in the not too distant future, not стоїть перед too. «Найближчим часом» — in the near future, а не in the nearest future (калька).

items.pattern: what the future holds (for sb) · nobody knows what the future holds · hold – held – held
items.meaning: what will happen in the future
items.example: When the factory closed, families in the town worried about **what the future held**.
more: Fortune tellers at the fair claim they can see **what the future holds**.
Who knows **what the future holds**? Maybe we'll live by the sea one day.
items.watchOut: «Що чекає в майбутньому» — what the future holds (for sb), не what the future has чи keeps. Можна й what the future will bring або what's in store for sb.

warmup.uk: Я хочу проводити більше часу з бабусею.
warmup.q: I want to ___ more time with my grandmother.
warmup.explain: Проводити час — spend time. Hold і conduct — «проводити» збори чи дослідження, а не час.

warmup.q: Could you tell me the ___, please?
warmup.explain: Котра година? — Could you tell me the time? Не the hour.

warmup.uk: Ми чудово провели час у Карпатах.
warmup.q: We ___ a great time in the Carpathians.
warmup.explain: Гарно провести час — have a good / great time. Spend a great time так не кажуть.

warmup.uk: Мені забракло часу, і я не доробив звіт.
warmup.q: I ___ time and couldn't finish the report.
warmup.explain: Не вистачило часу — run out of time. Run off — «утекти», а lack вживають без of.
Поставити будильник — set the alarm (set – set – set).

warmup.q: We're going to move in the ___ future.
warmup.explain: Найближчим часом — in the near future. Nearest — калька з «найближчим».

warmup.uk: Цей курс вартий твого часу й зусиль.
warmup.explain: Worth your (my, our) while — варте часу й зусиль, обов'язково з присвійним займенником.

warmup.uk: Не поспішай, потяг тільки о восьмій.
warmup.q: ___ your time: the train isn't until eight.

A.q: My dad ___ a lot of time in the garage fixing his old motorbike.
A.explain: Проводити час — spend time. Hold і conduct — «проводити» збори чи дослідження.

A.q: The cooking contestant ___ time before she could decorate her cake.
A.explain: Не вистачило часу — ran out of time. Run off — «утекти», а lack вживають без of.

A.q: The film started ___ on time, so the people who came late missed the beginning.
A.explain: Точно вчасно — bang / dead / right on time; bang і dead — розмовні.

B.q: We were having dinner when the fire alarm in the hotel ___ off.
B.explain: Спрацювала сигналізація, задзвонив будильник — the alarm went off. Ring off — «покласти слухавку».

B.q: It ___ me ages to tidy my son's room after the party.
B.explain: Це зайняло цілу вічність — it took (me) ages.

B.q: Everyone says the young violinist has a bright future ___ of her.
B.explain: Попереду — ahead of you (her, him). In front of потребує in, а forward of так не кажуть.

example.title: A week in the mountains
example.uk:
Минулого літа ми з сестрою провели тиждень у пішому поході шотландськими горами. Ми ставили будильники на пів на шосту, і щойно вони дзвонили, вискакували з ліжка. Ми йшли від світанку до смеркання.

Останнього вечора ми до глибокої ночі сиділи біля вогнища. Наступного ранку автобус до аеропорту приїхав хвилина в хвилину, але на дорогах були жахливі затори, і ми цілу вічність їхали через місто. Ми хотіли купити там подарунки, але нам забракло часу. Звісно ж, наш рейс затримали, тож ми скоротали час у кафе.

Іти було важко, але це було варте наших зусиль. Нам було так добре, як ніколи в житті, і ми плануємо повернутися туди в не надто далекому майбутньому.
example.en:
Last summer my sister and I [[spent a week|a1]] walking in the Scottish mountains. We [[set our alarms|b5]] for half past five, and as soon as they [[went off|b6]], we jumped out of bed. We walked [[from dawn till dusk|b7]].

On our last night we sat by the fire until [[the small hours|b8]]. Next morning the airport bus came [[bang on time|a10]], but the traffic was terrible and it [[took ages|b10]] to cross the city. We wanted to buy presents there, but we [[ran out of time|a14]]. Of course, our flight was delayed, so we [[killed time|a8]] in a café.

The walking was hard, but it was [[worth our while|b11]]. We [[had the time of our lives|a12]], and we're planning to go back [[in the not too distant future|b13]].
